Apply a two-input join AST node, dispatching on exec_mode

Source: R/execute.R
push_join.Rd

The join analogue of push_op() (D1). Joins can't reuse push_op() as-is because it is built around a single .data input: it reads exactly one exec_mode/ptr/schema to decide the schedule. A join has two independent inputs (x/y) whose either side being lazy forces the whole join lazy (mirroring the pre-unification behavior), and whose eager execution needs both sides' pointers anchored – see join_input_node().

Usage

push_join(
  join_type,
  x,
  y,
  join_spec,
  suffix,
  keep,
  na_matches,
  multiple = "all",
  unmatched = "drop",
  relationship = NULL,
  cross_by = FALSE
)

Arguments

join_type

One of "left", "inner", "full", "right", "semi", "anti", "cross"

x, y

The two tbl_gpu join inputs

join_spec

List with left/right/op/filter (and, when key types differ, key_casts), as returned by parse_join_by() / resolve_join_key_types()

suffix, keep, na_matches, multiple, unmatched, relationship

As documented on the join verbs (all are unused for "semi"/"anti", which have no suffix/keep/multiple/unmatched/relationship in dplyr's own signature; "cross" has none of keep/na_matches/ multiple/unmatched/relationship either, and always passes keep = TRUE internally purely to get build_join_output_info()'s all-common-names-suffixed behavior – see cross_join.tbl_gpu(), R/join.R)

cross_by

TRUE for dplyr's deprecated by = character() spelling: an ordinary join_type join over a constant key (see lower_cross_by_join(), R/lower.R)

Value

A new tbl_gpu

Details

Groups (F06): every dplyr join ends with dplyr_reconstruct(out, x), so for EVERY join type the result is grouped by intersect(x$groups, names(out)) and keeps x's .drop setting (x$group_drop); y's grouping is irrelevant. A group column that gets suffixed away (a name collision, or the key under keep = TRUE) simply drops out of the intersection; a merged key that is also a group column stays grouped (with its coerced type). Semi/anti outputs are x's schema verbatim, so all of x's groups survive.
